        I’m an undergraduate chemistry student at KAIST, conducting research in Prof. Woo Youn Kim’s group website. My current work combines molecular generative modeling with nonequilibrium statistical mechanics to estimate free-energy differences for molecular conformational ensembles.
      
      
        My research experience spans experimental materials chemistry, computational reaction mechanisms, and molecular machine learning. Across these areas, I’m interested in how molecular structure, local environments, and physical constraints shape chemical behavior.
      
      
        In the long term, I hope to apply these approaches to biological problems, including the molecular mechanisms of Alzheimer’s disease and the dynamics of intrinsically disordered proteins.

    Research Experience
    
      
        
          
            
              Intelligent Chemistry Lab website · KAIST
              Undergraduate Researcher
              Advisor: Prof. Woo Youn Kim
            
            
              Dec. 2025 - Present
            
          
          Neural Free-Energy Estimation for Molecular Ensembles
          
            Developing a free-energy estimation framework that uses a stochastic-interpolant model to propose transport paths between a harmonic reference and molecular Boltzmann distributions, with free-energy differences estimated from endpoint densities and forward–reverse path probabilities using Bennett acceptance ratio (BAR).
            Adapted and retrained DiTMC for Boltzmann-weighted ensemble generation and built the main inference pipeline, including transport kernels, work calculations, reverse-start sampling, BAR estimation, and diagnostic analyses.
          
          Full-Atom Antibody Design with Antigen Flexibility
          
            Investigated full-atom antibody design accounting for antigen flexibility and induced fit with an E(3)-equivariant generative framework.
            Designed and implemented auxiliary losses for atomic clashes and backbone and side-chain geometry, accounting for valid disulfide bonds; developed visualization and validation tools to assess structural accuracy and physical plausibility.
          
          AD-Agent: Mechanism-Aware Drug Repurposing for Alzheimer’s Disease
          
            Investigated mechanism-guided drug repurposing for Alzheimer’s disease using multi-agent reasoning.
            Implemented OpenTargets retrieval functions to integrate mechanistic and clinical evidence with traceable sources.
          
        
      

      
        
          
            
              Baik Group website · KAIST
              Undergraduate Researcher
              Advisor: Prof. Mu-Hyun Baik
            
            
              Jan. 2024 - Dec. 2025
            
          
          Brønsted Acid-Assisted Solid-State [2+2] Photocycloaddition
          Collaboration: Prof. Tehshik P. Yoon, University of Wisconsin–Madison
          
            Investigated how the local molecular environment and water influence selectivity and reactivity using DFT, molecular dynamics, and QM/MM calculations.
            Applied explicit-environment modeling to reproduce the observed diastereoselectivity that conventional DFT solvation models could not capture. Manuscript in preparation.
          
          Enantioselective Olefin 1,2-Arylamination with Chiral Indenyl–Rh Catalysts
          Collaboration: Prof. Simon B. Blakey, Emory University
          
            Investigated indenyl effects and how N-protecting groups modulate nitrogen nucleophilicity and chemoselectivity between arylamination and aziridination using DFT calculations.
            Proposed additional ligand controls, including saturated indenyl derivatives, to test the model of asymmetric orbital interactions underlying the indenyl effect. Published in ACS Catalysis (2026).
          
        
      

      
        
          
            
              Soft Material Assembly Group website · KAIST
              Undergraduate Researcher
              Advisor: Prof. Dong Ki Yoon
            
            
              Jun. 2023 - Dec. 2023
            
          
          Tunable Electrical Conductance Anisotropy in MOF–Polymer Composites
          
            Synthesized oxidation-sensitive Cu3(HHTP)2 and its derivatives, maintaining material quality and consistency for conductive MOF–polymer composites.
            Optimized voltage conditions for electric-field alignment of MOFs in a polymer matrix while avoiding solvent evaporation and material shortage in the ITO film. Published in Small (2024); featured on the front cover.
            Also investigated MOF–polymer composites as selective gas sensors.
          
        
      

      
        
          
            
              Choi Group · KSA
              Student Researcher
              Advisor: Prof. Eun Young Choi
            
            
              Apr. 2019 - Dec. 2021
            
          
          Activation and Adsorption Studies of MOFs and Zeolites
          
            Performed gas and ion exchange experiments on zeolite single crystals under high-vacuum conditions.
            Developed mild activation protocols for fragile porphyrin-based metal-organic frameworks to improve gas adsorption.
          
          Biocompatible Metal–Tartrate MOFs and Their Antibacterial Properties
          Singapore International Collaborative Research Program · Team Leader
          
            Synthesized Zn-, Co-, and Ag-tartrate MOFs through rapid room-temperature self-assembly and investigated their antibacterial properties.
